MyVenue.description:
One of the *viewer's own* venues on a shared strategy.

Two fields, because that is all the card renders. Deliberately not the full
mapping shape from `/exchange/mappings`: a listing must never carry another
user's venue, and the less it carries the less there is to leak.
MyVenue.title: MyVenue

PublishedRecord.description:
Forward performance of the venue a shared strategy publishes.

Deliberately has no Sharpe or max drawdown: those need a returns series, and
a figure synthesised from a handful of trades would sit next to the
backtest's years of data looking equally authoritative.
PublishedRecord.title: PublishedRecord

get.description:
Recent news articles, with optional symbol/sentiment/urgency filters.

Only articles that have been sentiment-tagged carry `sentiment` and
`urgency`; the same tagged rows are what the `NewsSentiment` indicator
reads, so this is the way to check an indicator will have data before
building a strategy on it.

`sort=impact` ranks by urgency, impact scope and tagger confidence
instead of publication time.

get.description:
A grid's detail, including every variation and its backtest results.

Ownership is checked against the row rather than the returned dict, which
carries no `user_id`. This route previously resolved the caller and then
ignored them — `grid_service.get_grid` filters on the id alone, so any
token could read any user's variations, parameters and results. Its
siblings `list_grids` and `archive_grid` were always scoped.

post.description:
Copy a strategy's logic into a new strategy owned by the caller.

A clone is *not* live. It carries no exchange mappings, so it reads as
paper, and taking it live means creating a live mapping — the copy itself
is just the indicators, rules and risk settings. The old "(Live)" suffix
and "promoted to live" message described the retired model where `mode`
was a column on the row.
